title: Review: Sol confirmation pass over the full A5 integration PR
description:
READ-ONLY REVIEW. Do not edit, create, or delete any file; do not commit; do not push. Your only writes are bd notes on this bead and closing it.

SCOPE: the full diff of branch eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8 against origin/main (`git diff origin/main...HEAD`) — one PR carrying eight beads: eshyra-o9bd.19.5.7.4 (character suffocation recovery gate, migration 0032, set_suffocation, calc breath formulas), eshyra-o9bd.19.5.7.5 (player-character death rules for encounter combatants, migration 0033), eshyra-o9bd.19.5.7.6 (adjust_hp knockOut), eshyra-o9bd.19.5.7.3 (adjust_exhaustion, derived level-4 HP maximum, level-6 death), eshyra-o9bd.19.5.11.4 (expend_ammunition / recover_ammunition, migration 0034), eshyra-o9bd.19.5.10.3 (roll_retained_check / resolve_retained_check / end_retained_check, set_surprised derived from comparisons, migration 0035), eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.6 (hydra Multiple Heads curated mechanic, tracked head count, derived reaction allowance, migration 0036), eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.5 (action:use-an-object ordinaryInteractionRuleRef -> rule:other-activity-on-your-turn, importer). Run `bd show` on each bead and on eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8 for the specs and acceptance criteria.

AUTHORITY: AGENTS.md; docs/design-and-pr-review-policy.md (profile rules-clause-complete); ADR 0020 §§2-3 (dice, arithmetic, atomic state mutation, resource accounting, state integrity are deterministic; adjudicated outcomes still pass through those boundaries); docs/design/rule-record-runtime-statements.md amendments A3-A5 and invariants 12-13; ADR 0015 (migration-first schema); docs/importer-fix-protocol.md for the importer parts; the committed SRD source text for every rule (packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1/records.json, records use the `key` field).

METHOD (review the mechanism, not the narrative):
1. For each capability, print the governing SRD source text beside the implementation and check source fidelity of every engine rule (thresholds, tie semantics, rounding, ordering, what counts as damage/healing, lifecycle start/end).
2. Check every model-facing surface (tool descriptions, schemas, Hybrid Contract in protocol.ts, known-limit statements in ruleKnownLimits.ts, error/rejection messages) against the real code: truthful, no model-side arithmetic/comparison or model-held canonical state offered as a fallback, target domain correct (character vs combatant), no stale wording from the pre-capability disclosures.
3. State integrity: atomicity (single transaction), invariants across the full state space (alive/dying/stable/dead, monster vs player-character rules, recovery block, exhaustion levels, closed vs active combat instances, missing/malformed rows), concentration and attunement side effects, campaign-actor sync, provenance conventions, deterministic ids/replay, write paths that bypass established helpers (mutateState, claimItem, removeItem), migration correctness (constraints, indexes, data preservation, contiguity, schema snapshot).
4. Write paths that let a model persist an unsupported/derived value (the A5 forbidden-substitution class), and any place a refusal could be bypassed through another tool (e.g. add_condition, update_combatant status, rest, level-up).
5. Test evidence: does each acceptance criterion have a test that distinguishes the bad state from the good state? Name missing evidence only where a real requirement is unprotected.
6. Sibling search: for each defect, look for the same class elsewhere in the diff.

REPORT with `bd update <this bead> --append-notes`, then `bd close <this bead>`. One entry per finding: ID (S1, S2, ...), severity (blocker / should-fix / nit), file:line, the violated requirement and its authority, a concrete failure scenario (inputs -> wrong state), and the minimal fix. Then a short list of what you checked and found correct. Apply the review policy's "From observation to finding" test: an observation without an operative requirement is "no requirement" in one line, not a finding. Do not stop at the first defect; batch everything you can find.

CONFIRMATION PASS. This is the second Sol review of this PR. The first (bead eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8.1, run `bd show eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8.1`) reported S1-S15 at 1165938c; repairs landed through eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8.2 (S1-S5, S11, S13), eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8.3 (S6-S10, S12, S14, S15), and supervisor commits (zero-maximum dying fix, eshyra-7vwa). For EACH of S1-S15, attack the repaired mechanism with new adversarial siblings (not only the original scenario) and state CLOSED or OPEN with evidence. Then review the new repair code itself (campaign_actor state_json lifecycle persistence and projection, schedule transfer, ammunition reservation in claim/give/list paths, long-rest ordering, level-up clamp, retained-check context listing, known-limit re-derivation, uniform halving with 0-HP lifecycle, injected gap registry) with the same method, and report any new finding in the same format (IDs continue from S16).
acceptance_criteria: Findings and S1-S15 closure recorded in bd notes; no file changes; bead closed by the reviewer.
notes:
Confirmation review at HEAD e601316cb8fbb270af5ddb9c9ebcd19a4e11766a, identical to integration branch eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8; base origin/main 18c1b30575d082afcc6c2df76e981bcb7be7a9d1. Full 77-file diff reviewed under rules-clause-complete, including repair decisions in .19.3.4.8.2/.3. Live Beads was used as authority; refs/beads/state is older and does not contain these integration/review rows. Governing committed SRD records were printed and compared with the implementations. Disposition: CHANGES REQUESTED. Six prior findings remain OPEN (S3, S4, S5, S8, S11, S14); three new findings follow as S16-S18. No other bead was changed.
S3 | OPEN | blocker | packages/core/src/state/encounterCombatants.ts:1978; :1922; :1958
Requirement/authority: SRD rule:death-saving-throws and rule:healing; .19.5.7.5 PC death lifecycle; .19.5.7.3 level-six death; ADR 0020 §§2-3. Repair bead .19.3.4.8.2 S3 explicitly requires exhaustion-six terminality for BOTH death-rule modes.
Fresh failures through the registry: (1) PC-rules combatant 20/20 -> update_combatant(hpDelta:-40,status:escaped or inactive) succeeds at 0 HP without instant death. The explicit-status branch still skips HP lifecycle derivation. Sibling: from dying at 0, hpDelta:-20,status:escaped suppresses instant death. (2) Ordinary lethal PC damage -> dead -> status:inactive -> hpDelta:1 succeeds as alive/1 HP: removal overwrites the only terminal-death marker. (3) Monster-rules combatant -> adjust_exhaustion(delta:6) is dead/10 HP -> hpDelta:1 becomes alive/10 HP with exhaustion still six, because the irreversible-exhaustion guard applies only to PC rules. Zero-head healing refusal works.
Minimal fix: derive mandatory damage/lifecycle outcomes before applying participation status; preserve terminal life state independently of removal/escape; apply exhaustion-six terminality in both modes. Keep the declared knockout exception and accepted ordinary monster revival behavior outside those mandatory conditions.
Permanent evidence: generalized invariant/transition matrix over death-rule mode, alive/dying/stable/dead, explicit statuses, lethal damage, and multi-step dead->inactive->heal. Proportionate because these are canonical death/revival violations. Owner: combatant lifecycle integration; material repair. Existing tests end at inactive and miss the next write.
S4 | OPEN | blocker | packages/core/src/state/encounterCombatants.ts:475; :1716; :1303
Requirement/authority: ADR 0020 state/identity integrity, durable campaign_actor ownership, .19.3.4.8.2 S4 atomic lifecycle continuity, and creature:hydra Multiple Heads (regrowth for heads lost since its last turn).
Fresh failure: recurring PC-rules hydra starts with five heads, loses one to 25 damage, then suffocates. begin_turn on its unavailable turn correctly commits two regrown heads and zero healing: combatant heads=6, actor.state.combatLifecycle.headCount=4. Actor sync runs only inside the healing call, which is suppressed. Closing and projecting the actor into a new encounter restores four heads, losing the committed regrowth and two reactions. This occurs with strictly increasing encounter timestamps, independently of S5.
Sibling: lose a head, close/reopen before the hydra's next own-turn end, then finish that turn. The new row has four heads/147 HP and regrows none because heads_died_since_own_turn and fire_damage_since_own_turn are not persisted/transferred; the source's pending regrowth is erased.
Minimal fix: sync all head settlements atomically even when actual healing is zero; retain/transfer the pending head-regrowth and suppression facts that survive the encounter boundary, rather than only current headCount. Preserve unrelated actor state.
Permanent evidence: generalized actor/projection parity across regrowth with and without a recovery block, and close/reopen before and after settlement, varying fire suppression. Proportionate to durable canonical state loss. Ordinary dying/counter/block/schedule continuity is repaired; S17 separately addresses external replacement of the reserved state. Owner: actor/head lifecycle integration; material repair.
S5 | OPEN | blocker | packages/core/src/state/encounterCombatants.ts:527; :1666
Requirement/authority: ADR 0020 canonical ownership/persistence; .19.3.4.8.2 S5 requires the actual current projection to own sync and stable recovery. Equal timestamps do not establish encounter ordering; ToolContext.at can be shared by multiple calls, and explicit combat instance ids are accepted inputs.
Fresh failures: open actor A in instance z, close it, then open A in instance a with the same timestamp. Damage in the active a projection changes its HP from 20 to 15 but syncCombatantActor skips it; actor HP remains 20 because z sorts higher lexically. With a stable actor instead, its deadline correctly transfers from z to a and is cleared on z, but resolveCombatantRecoveries(240) returns 0: the recovery query mistakes z for a newer projection and leaves the current stable actor at 0 HP past its deadline.
Minimal fix: establish actual projection ownership with a durable current-projection identity/ordering, and share that decision between sync and clock recovery; prioritize the current active projection and preserve legitimate recovery of the final closed projection. Do not use arbitrary ids as chronological tie-breakers.
Permanent evidence: generalized ownership invariant for equal timestamps and ascending/descending/custom/default ids, verifying actor sync and transferred recovery together. Proportionate because it silently loses canonical writes and recovery. Increasing-timestamp transfer and old schedule invalidation work; manual lifecycle refusal after closure is explicitly authorized. Owner: actor persistence integration; material repair.
S8 | OPEN | blocker | packages/core/src/state/encounterCombatants.ts:1231; :1279
Requirement/authority: SRD rule:healing and condition:exhaustion require current HP <= effective maximum; ADR 0020 state integrity. Repair bead .19.3.4.8.3 S8 expressly includes initialization/projection paths, not only projectToLiveCharacter.
Fresh failure: start_encounter with actor hpMax:20, hpCurrent:20, conditions:[{id:"exhaustion",level:4}] succeeds and persists both actor and combatant at 20 HP while the effective maximum is 10. Omitting hpCurrent defaults to the same invalid base maximum; a supplied/inherited exhausted actor takes the same path. The context renders HP 20/10.
Minimal fix: enforce the effective-maximum admission invariant on actor/combatant projection and relevant existing-state admission; clamp through a non-damage lifecycle boundary or explicitly refuse inconsistent input. Retain the base sheet maximum and do not turn a clamp into damage (S18).
Permanent evidence: generalized HP-bound invariant across supplied/defaulted/inherited actor HP, exhaustion below/above four, odd/even maxima, and zero-result lifecycle. Proportionate to persisted impossible state. Fresh level-up probes at exhaustion three/five and base maxima 22/25 pass, so the progression-specific repair is correct. Owner: HP/projection integration; material repair.
S11 | OPEN (silent fallback repaired; retry contract still false) | should-fix | packages/core/src/state/encounterCombatants.ts:1292; :1789; packages/core/src/state/actionEconomy.ts:442
Requirement/authority: .19.3.4.8.2 S11 adopts explicit bounded refusal for unknown historical head state and advertises closing/restarting as recovery; this review requires truthful error/rejection messages. ADR 0020 forbids inventing canonical head state.
Fresh failure: a pre-0036-shaped recurring hydra has head_count NULL. A permitted location-only update synchronizes combatLifecycle.headCount:null to its actor. Close its instance and start it again as the error instructs: the new projection inherits NULL, so begin_turn gives the same 'encounter began before head tracking; close ... and start it again' error forever, although that new encounter began after tracking. New damage/healing and turn-start refusal correctly prevent the old silent one-head fallback.
Minimal fix: make the unknown-state admission disposition and error agree. Preserve unknown history and give a truthful bounded refusal/repair instruction, or provide an explicitly authorized trustworthy repair path; do not silently reset a historical actor's heads to five merely to make retry work.
Permanent evidence: generalized unknown recurring-actor retry/admission test with harmless updates before closure, asserting either supported reconstructed state or truthful continued refusal. Proportionate localized contract/upgrade evidence. Owner: head lifecycle admission; non-material message repair if continued refusal is the chosen disposition.
S14 | OPEN (uniform halving and initial clamp repaired; zero-maximum recovery incomplete) | blocker | packages/core/src/state/hpLifecycle.ts:682; packages/core/src/state/encounterCombatants.ts:2005; :1673
Requirement/authority: uniform SRD condition:exhaustion halving, rule:healing's maximum, rule:death-saving-throws recovery, ADR 0020 lifecycle/state integrity, and .19.3.4.8.3 S14's explicit zero-HP lifecycle.
Fresh failures starting at base maximum/current HP 1 and applying exhaustion four: initial character and PC combatant clamps correctly enter dying at effective max 0. (1) record_death_save(roll:20) sets either target alive with hpCurrent:0 and reports 'revived', despite no HP regain. (2) PC combatant hpDelta:1 similarly sets alive/0 HP and resets counters. (3) stabilize that zero-max combatant and advance beyond its recovery deadline: the clock path writes alive/1 HP directly, exceeding effective max 0.
Minimal fix: make revival/counter reset depend on actual positive HP regained, and enforce effective maximum and lifecycle on automatic recovery as well as ordinary healing. Define the zero-maximum no-regain outcome consistently; do not restore the rejected minimum-one exception.
Permanent evidence: generalized HP/life-state invariant across characters/combatants, effective maxima zero/one/greater, natural-20/ordinary/stable-deadline recovery, with counters and persisted HP asserted. Proportionate because current writes falsely revive or exceed the maximum. Owner: shared HP lifecycle integration; material repair.
S16 | blocker | packages/core/src/state/ammunition.ts:103
Requirement/authority: .19.5.11.4's deterministic expenditure/recovery capability, SRD rule:weapon-properties (recovered ammunition returns to usable inventory), ADR 0020 resource accounting. S6's reservation is for unresolved expenditure, not a lifetime prohibition on firing a recovered physical item.
Failure through registry: give four arrows -> expend four in C1 -> close C1 -> recover two -> start C2 -> expend those two. The final call refuses 'inventory row ... is already accounted for as ammunition' and rolls back because alreadyTracked matches resolved historical rows too. Sibling: firing individual recovered one-piece rows also hits the guard on a full-row expenditure; splitting a larger recovered stack can postpone the failure until its last pieces.
Minimal fix: prohibit simultaneous unresolved accounting of a physical row, while allowing a new expenditure after prior settlement; preserve distinct expenditure identity and historical audit records, allocating a fresh physical drop row where necessary.
Permanent evidence: generalized two-battle recovery/re-expenditure invariant over whole/partial/single-piece rows, retaining the existing no-double-unresolved-accounting proof. Proportionate to an ordinary usable-inventory regression. Owner: ammunition accounting; localized behavioral repair.
S17 | blocker | packages/core/src/state/encounterCombatants.ts:1254; :1259; packages/core/src/orchestrator/toolStartEncounter.ts:70
Requirement/authority: .19.3.4.6 requires ENGINE-tracked head lifecycle and rejects model-supplied reaction totals; .19.3.4.8.2 S4 establishes a RESERVED engine-owned combatLifecycle subtree. ADR 0020 §§2-3 and design A5 prohibit model-written/model-held canonical substitutes.
Failure through the registered model surface: start_encounter actors[].state.combatLifecycle with deathRules:"monster", counters:0, recoveryBlock:null, stableRecovery:null, headCount:999 is schema-accepted and copied into the combatant. begin_turn grants reactionAllowance:999 for a normal source five-headed hydra. The supplied total write path has moved to a supplied canonical input. Sibling: after a recurring actor is opted into PC rules and suffocates, close/reopen it with actors[].state:{}; the subtree is deleted, and its 0-HP dying projection now has monster death rules and no suffocation block. Counters/schedules can likewise be replaced with structurally valid model values.
Minimal fix: reserve lifecycle state from ordinary model state input and preserve it independently when updating unrelated actor metadata. Initialize new canonical lifecycle inputs from source/engine transitions; allow any intentional repair only through its qualified operation, not the opaque state blob.
Permanent evidence: generalized tool-boundary invariant rejecting injection/removal/replacement of the reserved subtree while preserving unrelated actor state, including head allowance and suffocation continuity. Proportionate to canonical authority bypass. Owner: actor projection/head capability integration; material repair.
S18 | blocker | packages/core/src/state/exhaustionMutation.ts:130; :78
Requirement/authority: condition:exhaustion halves the maximum; this is not a damage event. SRD temporary-hit-points buffers damage, and creature:hydra loses heads only when it TAKES damage. .19.5.7.3 requires correct level-four HP state; ADR 0020 owns arithmetic and truthful persisted state.
Failure: character current/base max 20 with temporary HP 10 -> adjust_exhaustion(delta:4) calls adjustHp(-10). It consumes all temporary HP and leaves actual current HP 20 above effective max 10, while the tool falsely reports hpCurrent:10. Sibling: full-HP 172/172 hydra -> exhaustion four calls updateCombatant(hpDelta:-86), loses a head (5->4), records damage_this_turn:86 and a pending regrowth, even though exhaustion dealt no damage. Subsequent own-turn settlement can then generate healing from this invented injury.
Minimal fix: introduce/use a non-damage effective-maximum clamp that preserves temporary HP and does not feed damage-trigger accounting. Apply required zero-HP life/concentration/death side effects atomically, and return actual persisted HP.
Permanent evidence: generalized non-damage-clamp invariant over temporary HP absent/equal/exceeding the clamp and ordinary/multi-headed targets, including zero effective max and unchanged damage/head counters. Proportionate because one erroneous event classification corrupts several independently meaningful boundaries. Owner: exhaustion/HP lifecycle integration; material repair.

S12 CLOSED: food/water/speed entries retired; surprise names the wrong-tool trap; suffocation separates breath exhaustion from survival expiry. Six new CON boundary inputs (-5,-1,0,1,3,10) match source formulas, and permanent source-timing/statement tests pass.
S13 CLOSED for own-turn settlement: fresh skipped dying hydra regrows two heads and gains 20 HP; blocked variant commits six heads, gains zero HP and completes the boundary. Fire/dead cases and turn damage aggregation are covered and pass. Persistence of that result is the separate remaining S4 boundary.
S14 OPEN: maxima are halved uniformly and initial zero clamps enter the specified states; later recovery violates zero-maximum lifecycle as above.
S15 CLOSED: permanent injected fixture tests assert operation/owner/finding/unresolved work through the real producer. Fresh alternate shared-gap probe projects two rule keys and rejects an absent injected registration, so removal of nonempty projection is observable.
No requirement: unlimited retained-check context/enumeration beyond the explicitly adopted most-recent-20 contract.
No requirement: manual combatant death-save/stabilize/breathing mutations after encounter closure; .8.2 explicitly limits that state to clock-driven recovery.
No requirement: automatic death-save rolling by begin_turn, beyond the existing separately called death-save operation.
Checked and found correct, subject to the recorded findings:
- Character suffocation healing/stabilization/death-save gates, clearing on breathing/death, counter preservation, concentration/attunement hooks, and atomic rollback. Knockout consumes temporary HP first, overrides lethal overflow only when selected, arms stable recovery, and breaks concentration.
- Ordinary exhaustion increment/reduction/cap, level-six death transitions, final-maximum long-rest ordering, and repaired level-up/party projections.
- Ammunition reservations, ordinary even/odd/mixed-identity settlement, location/battle checks, canonical custody/destruction helpers and atomic resolution. Recovery and expenditures retain attributable deterministic identities.
- Retained totals are not rerolled; fresh search/passive calculations use strict observer-win tie semantics, validated campaign/participant identities and persisted comparisons. Supplied surprise lists/reaction totals are rejected on their direct tool surfaces. Surprise first-turn enforcement, roll visibility, trace/ledger integration and report-gap injection were inspected.
- Source hydra curation matches five initial heads, 25-damage per-turn threshold, two regrown heads per lost head, fire suppression, ten HP per regrown head and opportunity-attack-only extra reactions. Ordinary turn aggregation/loss/regrowth and terminal zero-head guard work.
- Use-an-object relationship reaches the free-interaction rule:other-activity-on-your-turn. Only intended generated record changes occur. Migrations 0032-0036 are contiguous; constraints/index/data-preservation and generated snapshot/parity evidence pass.

Validation at reviewed HEAD: npm run typecheck passed (forced build); npm run check passed without fixes; npm run test passed: 5672 passed / 3 documented skipped, 320 passed / 2 skipped test files. npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-pack reproduced all 1799 records with zero added/removed/changed records, unchanged manifest, and exact source inventory/coverage/region ledger/provenance/relationship artifacts. Throwaway /tmp node/tsx probes supplied the fresh adversarial evidence above. Git diff/status confirm no tracked changes; no commit, push or PR write was made. Only this review bead receives notes and closure; it records completed review, not implementation approval.
